column1: # Game profile of Chained Echoes (Switch, update 1.1.1 = v131072). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2020.3.36f1 (IL2CPP), SDK 14.3.0 (its sdk is Batman: Arkham Knight 1.0.5's build, 2aef2cff…), NVN API 55.15; subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie.
# The shaders are Unity shader objects in the player's serialized files and packs under Data/, read by the shader split: 3,832 of them (1,877 vertex, 1,881 pixel, 73 compute, 1 geometry).
# The game asks for present interval 1 and runs at 60 fps on the Mac, as on the Switch.
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: the game takes its memory as address regions. The sdk build takes the SDK-wide node area cut
# (1 GB → 62 MB) and the 2 MB alignment of large regions (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py, implementation 3 of 8 and 3 of 4). The 5 GB block of Ace Attorney Investigations Collection with a
# 3.2 GB pool: the alias region's high-water mark was +3.5 GB of the 64 GB alias region in a 2-minute play run, 1.95 GB resident and 1.01 GB of Metal allocations.
# The pool is still the survey's guess: no heap check has run on this build (the profile entered the tools through DM_GAMES_DIR, so the NSP script did not treat it as provisional).
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and its bundles
